todos.description: Always write the XMP sidecar, including for a JPEG that has no RAW pair
todos.context: Today an XMP sidecar is only ever written, read, copied or deleted for the RAW half of a pair: every write site is gated on photo.HasRAW() and the path comes from model.SidecarPath(photo.RAWPath) (saveSidecar in internal/gui/app/tags_action.go, plus the backgrounded run, typed-fallback and exit-flush paths in internal/gui/app/tags_runs.go), while reads merge through imaging.mergedWithSidecar and the library copier/deleter touch the sidecar only alongside the RAW file. Dropping that restriction means a JPEG with no RAW pair gets a sidecar named after the JPEG, so the sidecar path needs a photo-based source rather than RAWPath alone and the file must also be read back, copied and deleted for JPEG-only photos. CLAUDE.md documents the opposite rule today ("a JPEG without a RAW pair is never written to on its own"), so that prose changes with the behaviour; the in-place JPEG XMP packet write stays behind Save JPEG regardless.

plan.summary: Today the XMP sidecar is bound to the RAW half of a pair: every read (mergedWithSidecar), every write (tagsSession.saveSidecar, plus finishDetached, saveTyped, tagRunner.saveSidecar and flushTyped in the runner), and the copier/deleter sidecar handling are gated on photo.HasRAW() with the path taken from model.SidecarPath(photo.RAWPath). The change makes the sidecar belong to the photo instead of to the RAW: a new model.Photo.SidecarPath() returns the RAW-derived path when there is a pair (identical to today's, since the pair shares a basename) and the image-derived path otherwise, and every gate on HasRAW() around sidecar work is dropped. The work is sequenced from the model outwards - path helper, read path, dialog write path, background-run write paths, copier, deleter, the copy/delete wait in the app - each step carrying its own tests, with the CLAUDE.md prose that states the opposite rule updated last.

steps.title: Give model.Photo a sidecar path of its own
steps.details: Add `func (p Photo) SidecarPath() string` to `internal/core/model/photo.go`: return `SidecarPath(p.RAWPath)` when `p.HasRAW()`, otherwise `SidecarPath(p.ImagePath)`. Keep the package-level `SidecarPath(path string)` (it stays the pure extension-swap helper and is still used by tests and by the copier for a RAW path); widen its doc comment so it no longer claims the sidecar belongs to a RAW alone - the sidecar is the app's own store for the photo, named after the RAW when there is one so Lightroom and Bridge find it, and after the image when there is not. Extend `internal/core/model/photo_test.go` (`TestSidecarPath` area) with a table for the method: paired photo -> `/photos/DSC001.xmp` from the RAW, JPEG-only -> `/photos/DSC001.xmp` from the JPEG, uppercase `.JPG`, and a PNG. Nothing calls the method yet, so behaviour is unchanged.

steps.title: Read the sidecar for every photo, not only for a RAW pair
steps.details: In `internal/core/imaging/stock_info.go` drop the `if !photo.HasRAW() { return info, nil }` early return in `mergedWithSidecar` and read `photo.SidecarPath()`; a missing file is already an empty, error-free read in `ReadSidecar`. Update the surrounding prose: the `GetStockInfo` comment ("and, when the photo has a RAW pair, the sidecar written next to it"), the `StockInfo.complete` field comment ("the XMP sidecar of a RAW pair") and the `mergedWithSidecar` comment. Update the two comments in `internal/core/imaging/image_provider.go` that speak of "the XMP sidecar of a RAW pair" (`StockInfo` doc, `PeekStockDate` doc) - no code change there. Tests: in `internal/core/imaging/stock_info_test.go` add a case alongside `TestExifService_GetStockInfo_ReadsTheSidecarBehindABrokenPacket` where a JPEG with no `.ARW` next to it has a sidecar and the sidecar tags win over the EXIF/packet ones; in `internal/core/imaging/image_provider_test.go` add a subtest to `TestImageProvider_StockInfo` mirroring "the sidecar beats the tags of the JPEG" for a photo with an empty `RAWPath` (a real temp dir is needed, unlike the existing `/photo.jpg` cases).

steps.title: Let the Tags dialog write the sidecar of a JPEG-only photo
steps.details: In `internal/gui/app/tags_action.go`, `tagsSession.saveSidecar`: drop `!s.photo.HasRAW()` from the guard (the `written.Equal(s.saved)` and `nothingToWrite` conditions stay) and take `path := s.photo.SidecarPath()`. Adjust the function's comment block, which currently implies the file is the RAW's. Tests: in `internal/gui/app/tags_runs_test.go` switch the shared helpers `sidecarTags`, and in `internal/gui/app/tags_action_test.go` `writeTestSidecar`/`awaitSidecar` plus the inline `imaging.ReadSidecar(model.SidecarPath(photo.RAWPath))` in `TestTagsSessionCloseWithAConceptAlone`, to `photo.SidecarPath()` so they work for both kinds of photo; add a case to `internal/gui/app/tags_action_test.go` that types into a dialog for `testPhoto(t, false)`, closes it, and asserts the sidecar named after the JPEG holds the typed tags (and that reopening the dialog seeds from it).

steps.title: Let a backgrounded, failed or flushed run write the sidecar too
steps.details: In `internal/gui/app/tags_runs.go`: in `finishDetached` remove the `if !run.photo.HasRAW() { r.report(...); r.release(run); return }` branch so every landed run goes through `r.saveSidecar`, and delete the now-unused `report` helper (golangci-lint's unused check would flag it); in `saveTyped` reduce the guard to `nothingToWrite(typed)` and take the name from `filepath.Base(run.photo.SidecarPath())`; in `tagRunner.saveSidecar` and in `flushTyped` take `run.photo.SidecarPath()` and drop `!run.photo.HasRAW()` from the flush guard. Update the comments that call the sidecar the RAW pair's. Tests in `internal/gui/app/tags_runs_test.go`: add a JPEG-only (`testPhoto(t, false)`) variant of "a backgrounded run keeps going and saves what it found" asserting the sidecar next to the JPEG, and a JPEG-only variant of the exit-flush test (`stopAll` writing the handed-over fields); check the existing subtests that assert `NoFileExists` still use `testPhoto(t, true)` where the assertion is about a cancelled run rather than about a missing RAW.

steps.title: Keep the sidecar copy tied to the RAW
steps.details: Decided against the earlier draft: the sidecar travels only when the RAW does. `copyRAW` keeps calling `copySidecar`, `CopyJPEGOnly` keeps taking no sidecar, and a JPEG with no RAW pair leaves its own sidecar behind in every mode - what is copied is the image, and the tags stay with the file they were written for. No production change in `internal/core/library/copier.go`; add `TestCopier_LeavesTheSidecarOfAJPEGWithoutARAW` to `copier_test.go` (CopyJPEGOnly and CopyWithRAW, JPEG copied, `photo.xmp` left behind) so the rule is guarded rather than implied.

steps.title: Delete the sidecar with the photo unless a RAW is left behind
steps.details: In `internal/core/library/deleter.go` take the sidecar removal out of the `includeRAW && photo.HasRAW()` block: remove `photo.SidecarPath()` whenever the image is deleted and no RAW pair is being kept - i.e. when `!photo.HasRAW() || includeRAW` - so a JPEG-only photo leaves no orphan while a bulk delete that keeps the RAWs keeps the sidecar that describes them. Change `removeSidecar` to take the photo (or the path) and rewrite its comment. Tests in `internal/core/library/deleter_test.go`: keep "the sidecar stays when the RAW is kept", and add two subtests for a photo with an empty `RAWPath` - its sidecar goes with `Delete`, and it goes with `DeleteWithOption(photo, false)` as well since there is no RAW to keep it for.

steps.title: Leave the copy wait as it is, fix the comment
steps.details: Follows from the copy decision: `copyPhotoFiles` in `internal/gui/app/actions.go` keeps waiting only when `photo.HasRAW() && mode != library.CopyJPEGOnly`, because only a copy that takes the RAW takes a sidecar with it. The comment above the gate is the one thing that changes: a run now writes the sidecar of any photo, so it can no longer be called the RAW pair's alone. No test change.

steps.title: Update the documented rule in CLAUDE.md
steps.details: Rewrite the sidecar sentences in the Stock tags bullet: the parenthetical "(a JPEG without a RAW pair is never written to on its own - that stays behind Save JPEG)" becomes the new rule - the sidecar is written next to the photo, named after the RAW when there is a pair and after the image when there is not, while the in-place XMP packet write of the JPEG itself still stays behind Save JPEG. Adjust the neighbouring clauses that say the sidecar is copied with, or deleted with, the RAW (the copy/delete sentences in the same bullet), and mention in the Delete bullet that the sidecar goes with the photo unless a RAW pair is kept.

questions.question: Sidecar name for a JPEG with no RAW pair: assume the extension is swapped (`DSC001.JPG` -> `DSC001.xmp`, the same name a pair would use) unless you want the exiftool/digiKam style `DSC001.JPG.xmp` - affects step 1 and everything after it.
questions.answer: DSC001.xmp - the extension is swapped, the same name a pair would use.

questions.question: Copying a paired photo as "Photo" (CopyJPEGOnly): assume the sidecar now travels with the JPEG too (it is the photo's tag store), which flips an existing test expectation - say so if the sidecar should keep staying behind in that mode (step 5).
questions.answer: No - copying a paired photo as "Photo" (CopyJPEGOnly) leaves the sidecar behind, as today.

questions.question: Deleting with "Delete with RAW files" unchecked for a paired photo: assume the sidecar stays, because it also holds the kept RAW's develop settings (step 6). Yes/no?
questions.answer: Yes - the sidecar stays when the RAW is kept; it also holds the kept RAW's develop settings.

questions.question: Non-JPEG photos (`.png` is in the scanner's supported set): assume they get a sidecar under the same rule (steps 2-4), since the code paths are shared.
questions.answer: Yes - a .png gets a sidecar under the same rule; the code paths are shared.

questions.question: For a JPEG-only photo the sidecar now outranks the XMP packet inside the JPEG on read (FillMissing puts the sidecar first). Assume that is wanted - i.e. tags edited in another tool inside the JPEG lose to our sidecar until Save JPEG is pressed - unless you prefer the packet to win for JPEG-only photos (step 2).
questions.answer: Yes - the sidecar wins over the JPEG packet for a JPEG-only photo too, the same merge rule as pairs.

questions.question: Should the sidecar of a JPEG with no RAW pair travel with a "Photo + RAW" copy?
questions.answer: No - the sidecar is copied only when a RAW exists and is copied with it. A JPEG-only photo leaves its sidecar behind in every mode.

risks: Two supported images sharing a basename in one folder (`DSC001.JPG` and `DSC001.PNG`) would share a single sidecar and overwrite each other's tags; the extension-swap naming makes that unavoidable.

An orphan sidecar left next to a JPEG by an older version (RAW deleted, sidecar kept, or a Lightroom sidecar for a RAW that moved away) now becomes authoritative for that JPEG and can resurrect stale tags in the dialog.
Every JPEG-only photo now costs one extra file read in `completeStock`/`GetStockInfo`; noticeable only on slow or network volumes, and it happens on a worker goroutine.

Existing tests assert `NoFileExists` on sidecars for photos built with `testPhoto(t, false)`; the runner change in step 4 makes those paths write, so any such assertion that was really about a cancelled run must be moved to a paired photo or re-read.

The `StockInfo.complete` flag and the seed/prefill dance in `tagsSession` assume a read that skipped the sidecar was still complete for a JPEG-only photo; step 2 makes the read do real I/O there, so a sidecar that fails to parse now surfaces as an error on photos that never reported one before.

todos.description: Save the Editorial flag and its date with the tags, the way the Concept note already is
todos.context: The Concept note rides on model.Tags.Concept (counted by Equal but deliberately not by IsEmpty) and is persisted through the paired tables in internal/core/imaging/sidecar.go - ownedProperties for reading, writtenProperties for writing - which internal/core/imaging/xmp_packet.go reuses for the JPEG XMP packet, while the pure-EXIF fallback cannot carry it and only reports ConceptDropped; reads merge packet over sidecar in stock_info.go. On the GUI side TagsDialog.SetPhotoInfo/showTags/takeConcept/RestoreTags restore the note without overwriting text the user typed first, fed from imaging.StockInfo through the per-photo cache in internal/gui/app/tags_action.go. The Editorial check and its date entry live only in the dialog today and only feed the prompt line built by Notes()/editorialDate(): no editorial flag or editorial date is in metadata anywhere, and StockInfo.Taken is the EXIF shooting date, which merely seeds the entry as defaultDate.

plan.summary: Persist the Tags dialog's Editorial checkbox and its date the same way the Concept note is persisted: as `photo:` properties in the XMP sidecar and in the JPEG XMP packet, carried on `model.Tags` so every existing writer/reader path (dialog close, generation run, hand-over on close, exit flush, Save JPEG, cache seeding) picks them up for free. `model.Tags` gains an `Editorial` value (marked flag + day) that `Equal` counts but `IsEmpty` deliberately ignores, exactly like `Concept`; `internal/core/imaging/sidecar.go` gains one `ownedProperty` and one `writtenProperty` pair per field (read/write), which `xmp_packet.go` reuses unchanged; `stock_info.go` fills it level by level like the place; the pure-EXIF fallback cannot carry it and reports it dropped like the concept. On the GUI side the dialog's `Tags()` reports the checkbox and the date entry, `SetPhotoInfo`/`showTags` tick the box and seed the entry from the file without overwriting a box the user already touched, `RestoreTags` puts a handed-over state back whole, and `tags.Request` carries the flag so a generation echoes it back into the tags it saves. The editorial date is normalised to a UTC calendar day everywhere so that a round trip through the file compares equal and does not rewrite the sidecar on every close.

steps.title: Add the editorial flag and date to model.Tags
steps.details: In internal/core/model/tags.go add a small value type beside Place: `type Editorial struct { Marked bool; Date time.Time }` with `Normalized() Editorial` (returns the zero value when !Marked; otherwise the Date reduced to its calendar day at midnight UTC via time.Date(y, m, d, 0,0,0,0, time.UTC), zero Date left zero) and `IsEmpty() bool { return !e.Marked }`. Normalisation is the point: the dialog's date can arrive as an EXIF shooting time, as a UTC midnight from the typed-text parser, or as whatever the Fyne calendar hands back, and unnormalised values would never compare equal to the day read back from the file, so every close would rewrite the sidecar. Add the field `Editorial Editorial` to Tags. Extend `Tags.Equal` with `t.Editorial.Normalized() == other.Editorial.Normalized()` (all normalised values carry loc==UTC and no monotonic clock, so == is exact). Leave `IsEmpty` and `Problems` untouched, and extend the existing comment above IsEmpty to say the editorial flag is ignored there for the same reason as the concept: it is not something a generation produces, so a flag alone must not pass for a result. Tests in internal/core/model/tags_test.go beside the existing Equal/IsEmpty cases: a flag alone is still IsEmpty; Equal separates two Tags that differ only by the flag or by the day; Normalized drops the time of day, drops the date when unmarked, and makes two times of the same day on different locations compare equal.

steps.title: Read and write the flag through the sidecar tables
steps.details: In internal/core/imaging/sidecar.go add the constants `editorialProperty = "Editorial"`, `editorialDateProperty = "EditorialDate"` and a layout const for the value (time.DateOnly, i.e. 2026-06-13 - XMP's date form, day precision). Reading: give `sidecarTags` an `editorial model.Editorial` field and add two entries to `ownedProperties`, both under photoNamespace: Editorial, whose read parses the text case-insensitively as a boolean (strconv.ParseBool covers True/true/1) into `s.editorial.Marked`, and EditorialDate, whose read parses time.DateOnly (falling back to time.RFC3339 for a document written by another tool) into `s.editorial.Date` and ignores an unparsable value. `sidecarTags.tags()` returns `Editorial: s.editorial.Normalized()`, so a date without a flag is dropped on read the same way it is on write. Writing: append two entries to the end of `writtenProperties`, after the concept and with the same photoPrefix/photoNamespace, both emitted with writeTextProperty: Editorial with `values` returning []string{"True"} when `tags.Editorial.Normalized().Marked` and nil otherwise, and EditorialDate returning the day formatted with the layout when marked and the date is non-zero. Appending under the existing photo prefix keeps `namespaceBindings` and therefore `ownDescriptionPattern()` byte-identical, so descriptions written by earlier versions stay recognisable and are still edited in place - move/extend the "Last on purpose" comment so it reads as a statement about the photo-prefixed block rather than about the concept alone. No change is needed to stripPatterns: `photo:Editorial\b` cannot match `photo:EditorialDate` (l and D are both word characters, so there is no boundary between them), which is worth a test of its own. Tests in internal/core/imaging/sidecar_test.go, mirroring TestWriteSidecar_Concept as TestWriteSidecar_Editorial: a new sidecar carries the two properties and reads back Equal; a sidecar without the flag declares no photo namespace; the flag and the date are replaced rather than doubled on a second save; clearing the flag leaves neither property behind; a flag alone is written without any tags; a Lightroom sidecar keeps its crs settings; and - the regression guard - clearing only the date leaves `photo:Editorial` standing while removing `photo:EditorialDate`.

steps.title: Merge the flag on read and cover the JPEG packet
steps.details: In internal/core/imaging/stock_info.go extend `FillMissing` level by level, next to the concept line: take `fallback.Editorial.Marked` when the newer set is not marked, and `fallback.Editorial.Date` when the newer date is zero, then keep the result normalised. This gives the packet-over-sidecar merge in GetStockInfo/stockInfoFromSegments the same semantics the concept has. No production change is needed in internal/core/imaging/xmp_packet.go - packetWithTags goes through sidecarProperties/stripProperties/writtenBindings - but add TestPacketWithTags_Editorial to xmp_packet_test.go beside TestPacketWithTags_Concept: a padded camera packet takes the flag and the date and parses back to them, a packet with too little padding is refused (ok == false) so the caller falls back to the EXIF, and clearing the flag removes both properties and the description an earlier save appended. Tests in internal/core/imaging/stock_info_test.go beside the concept cases: a JPEG whose packet carries the flag reports it; a sidecar that carries it wins over a packet that carries a different day; a sidecar that carries no flag keeps the packet's.

steps.title: Report the flag the EXIF fallback cannot carry
steps.details: In internal/core/imaging/exif_write.go add `EditorialDropped bool` to StockWrite beside ConceptDropped, extend the comment above them to name the third field the EXIF has no place for, and set it in WriteStockTags's fallback return as `tags.Editorial.Normalized().Marked`. stockEntries and exifShadows stay as they are: the EXIF carries the title and the keywords only. Tests in internal/core/imaging/exif_write_test.go beside TestExifService_WriteStockTags_Concept: a JPEG with a roomy packet takes the flag and reports EditorialDropped false; a JPEG whose packet has no room reports EditorialDropped true, the file is rewritten and reading it back shows no editorial flag; a write of tags without the flag reports false.

steps.title: Echo the flag back from a generation
steps.details: In internal/core/tags/tagger.go add `Editorial model.Editorial` to Request and, in the success branch of Generate where the location and the concept are taken back from the request, set `generated.Editorial = req.Editorial.Normalized()`. This is what keeps the flag in the file when a run finishes: runFinished and the detached finishDetached both write the *generated* tags to the sidecar and the cache, with no dialog field folded in, so a flag missing from the generated set would be erased from the sidecar the moment a generation lands. The prompt text is untouched - Notes() already spells the Editorial line. Tests in internal/core/tags/tagger_test.go beside the concept case: a request that carries the flag gets it back on the generated tags, normalised to the day; a request without it produces tags with an empty Editorial; a failed run is unaffected.

steps.title: Let the dialog report the flag as part of its tags
steps.details: In internal/gui/ui/tags_dialog.go add `func (d *TagsDialog) Editorial() model.Editorial` returning the zero value when the box is unchecked and otherwise `model.Editorial{Marked: true, Date: *d.date.Date}` (zero Date when d.date.Date is nil), normalised. Use it in `Tags()` as the new `Editorial:` field and rewrite `Notes()`/`editorialDate()` to format that value instead of reading the widgets directly, so the prompt line and the saved value can never disagree; the prompt keeps the "January 2, 2006" layout and the existing "Editorial:" bare-flag form. From this step on, closing the dialog after ticking the box writes the sidecar through the existing saveSidecar path, because Tags.Equal now separates the two states. Tests in internal/gui/ui/tags_dialog_test.go: a ticked box with the seeded date makes Tags().Editorial marked on the right day with no time of day; an unticked box leaves Tags().Editorial empty even though the date entry still holds the shooting date; ticking and clearing the date gives a marked value with a zero date; the existing Notes() cases still produce "Editorial: August 18, 2026" and the bare "Editorial:".

steps.title: Put the saved flag back on the dialog
steps.details: Still in internal/gui/ui/tags_dialog.go, restore what the file holds without overwriting what the user did first, the way takeConcept does for the note: add `editorialTouched` and a `settingEditorial` guard to TagsDialog - the check's OnChanged (extracted from the inline closure in buildInputs into a method) shows/hides the date row as today and sets editorialTouched when the change did not come from the dialog itself, and a helper setEditorialChecked wraps `d.editorial.SetChecked` in the guard. `takeEditorial(model.Editorial)` ticks the box when the file says marked, the user has not touched it, and it is not already ticked; it never unticks, since a box left off is indistinguishable from one never seen. In SetPhotoInfo, seed the date from the saved editorial day when the file has one and from `taken` otherwise (`seed := taken; if date := existing.Editorial.Date; !date.IsZero() { seed = date }`), keeping the existing dateUntouched()/defaultDate guard, so the day the user chose last time wins over the shooting date and the second SetPhotoInfo call (seed then prefill) does not flip the entry back and forth. Call takeEditorial from showTags and from the tags-less branch of SetPhotoInfo, beside takeConcept - a flag with no tags is worth restoring, like a note with no tags. `RestoreTags` puts the handed state back whole, as it does for the location and the note: setEditorialChecked(handed.Editorial.Marked), set the date entry when the handed value carries one, and mark editorialTouched (and the date as no longer untouched) so a prefill read landing afterwards cannot tick a box the closing dialog had cleared. SetTags and PasteTags stay as they are: a run has nothing to add to the user's own field, and a paste carries the title and the keywords only. Tests in internal/gui/ui/tags_dialog_test.go beside the concept ones: a file whose tags carry the flag ticks the box, shows the date row and puts its day into the entry, in preference to the shooting date; a box the user ticked survives a later SetPhotoInfo that says unmarked; a box ticked by the file is not re-ticked after the user clears it and a second read lands; RestoreTags of an unmarked value clears a box the seed had ticked; RestoreTags of a marked value with a day fills the entry.

steps.title: Wire the app: generation request, worth-a-sidecar and the dropped note
steps.details: In internal/gui/app/tags_action.go: pass `Editorial: s.dialog.Editorial()` in the tags.Request that generate() builds, so a run echoes it back (step 5) and a backgrounded or detached run writes it; extend `nothingToWrite` with `&& tags.Editorial.IsEmpty()` and its comment, so an editorial flag alone is worth a sidecar the way a note alone is (this also covers the hand-over and exit-flush paths in tags_runs.go, which call nothingToWrite and need no change of their own); add `editorialDroppedNote` beside conceptDroppedNote and append it in writeNote when `write.EditorialDropped`. Update the Stock tags paragraph of CLAUDE.md that describes the Concept note being saved so it names the editorial flag and its date as saved the same way - `photo:Editorial` and `photo:EditorialDate` in the sidecar and in the JPEG packet, a flag alone worth a sidecar, and the EXIF fallback saying it cannot carry it. Tests in internal/gui/app/tags_action_test.go: add editorial rows to the TestNothingToWrite table (a marked flag is worth writing, an unmarked value with a date is not); extend TestWriteNote with EditorialDropped alone and in combination; add a session test in the shape of TestTagsSessionCloseWithAConceptAlone - type a marked Editorial into the dialog, close, await the sidecar, reopen and assert the box comes back ticked on the same day - and a run test in internal/gui/app/tags_runs_test.go asserting that a backgrounded run started from a dialog with the box ticked writes the flag into the sidecar it saves.

questions.question: Property names and values: assume `photo:Editorial` with the XMP boolean text "True" and `photo:EditorialDate` with a day-precision `2026-06-13`, both omitted entirely when the box is unchecked, unless you want a different spelling (e.g. a single property holding the date) - affects step 2.
questions.answer: photo:Editorial with the boolean text "True" and photo:EditorialDate with a day-precision 2026-06-13; both omitted when the box is unchecked.

questions.question: Model shape: assume a `model.Editorial{Marked bool; Date time.Time}` value on Tags rather than two flat fields `Editorial bool` / `EditorialDate time.Time`; say so if you prefer the flat pair - affects step 1 and every later step's field access.
questions.answer: model.Editorial{Marked bool; Date time.Time} beside Place, not a flat pair.

questions.question: Assume the editorial date is stored day-precision only (time of day dropped, normalised to UTC) - a full timestamp would make the sidecar disagree with itself after a round trip and rewrite on every close. Affects steps 1 and 2.
questions.answer: Yes - day precision only, normalised to UTC.

questions.question: Assume Alt+C / Alt+V still carry the title and the keywords only, so the editorial flag stays with the photo it was ticked for, like the place and the note - affects nothing today but confirms tags_clipboard.go is untouched.
questions.answer: Yes - Alt+C / Alt+V still carry the title and the keywords only; tags_clipboard.go is untouched.

questions.question: Assume the pure-EXIF fallback gets its own `EditorialDropped` note ("the editorial flag was not written...") beside the concept one, rather than one merged sentence - affects steps 4 and 8.
questions.answer: Yes - its own EditorialDropped note beside the concept one.

risks: The two new properties cost about 90 more bytes in the JPEG XMP packet, so a photo whose packet padding was only just big enough will now fall through to the EXIF rewrite path (file replaced, camera re-index warning) when the flag is set. Only Save JPEG is affected.

FillMissing gives the flag the same semantics the concept has: a flag cleared in the sidecar comes back from a JPEG packet that still carries it, until Save JPEG is pressed again. Deliberate, but worth a test comment.

Timezone/precision: any path that puts an unnormalised time.Time into Tags.Editorial (the Fyne calendar returns a local time, the typed-text parser a UTC one) would make Equal false forever and rewrite the sidecar plus show a "Tags saved" notification on every dialog close. Normalisation must sit in the model and be applied by the dialog accessor, the sidecar reader and the tagger.

The strip regexes match on the prefixed name, so `photo:Editorial` and `photo:EditorialDate` must stay distinguishable; the `\b` in the existing patterns does that, but only because no word boundary exists between "Editorial" and "Date" - a rename such as `photo:Editorial-Date` would silently break the strip and double the property.

New writtenProperties entries must be appended under the existing photo prefix; inserting one that introduces a new prefix, or reordering, changes ownDescriptionPattern() and would stop the writer from recognising and editing in place the descriptions earlier versions appended to sidecars and packets.

Overlaps with todo #16 (always write the sidecar): both touch tagsSession.saveSidecar in internal/gui/app/tags_action.go, so whichever lands second will need a small rebase - no functional dependency.
